paths.description: Homepage and global chrome; represents primary discovery, consent, navigation and content-card template.
Store deals listing; represents commerce/category cards, pricing and FAQ content.
Surface Laptop detail; represents the prominent product-detail and purchase journey.
Microsoft 365 landing page; represents subscription/product-family marketing and no-JS content.
Microsoft AI category; represents an editorial/business-solution landing template.
Global search opening and input; represents the primary inline form control.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-colour preference.
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the page reports color-scheme: normal and keeps body background rgb(255,255,255); the dark screenshot remains light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and supply preference-driven surface/text tokens, using light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: Page and state navigation has no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The rendered CSS probe found zero view-transition rules across the home page, while navigation is a core part of this multi-page site.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin template navigation, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The optional-cookie notice consumes substantial space before the main content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show the cookie notice before the global header and hero, occupying roughly 300 px desktop and 215 px mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface with equal Accept/Reject actions and persist the choice.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport adaptation rather than container-aware reuse.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero @container rules across the rendered homepage; the page has repeated card components used in several widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card groups containment and adapt card composition with size container queries.

findings.summary: A prominent Surface shopping path dead-ends on a demand error.
findings.evidence: The representative Surface Laptop product URL returned “Thank you for your patience… high demand” instead of product details or purchase actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore the product route and provide a reliable cached or alternate product-detail path when the upstream is overloaded.

findings.summary: The product-route failure offers no actionable recovery.
findings.evidence: The failure page says “wait and try again later” but provides no retry control, status link, product-list fallback, or way back to the relevant Surface category.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Retry, product-list, support/status, and back-navigation actions while preserving the user’s context.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance misses the Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 17.2 s, TBT 405 ms, Speed Index 11.0 s, and interactive at 25.6 s; the independent trace measured LCP 2.83 s and 61 ms TBT, showing substantial run-to-run load sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce critical request chains, and defer non-essential scripts; remeasure under controlled mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Main-thread work delays readiness.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 405 ms TBT; the trace recorded two long tasks, including one 111 ms task.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, schedule non-critical work by priority, and defer analytics/store-assistant initialization.

findings.summary: The homepage has a large, script-heavy critical load.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 197 requests and 3.01 MB transferred, including 140 scripts (1.74 MB) and multiple VeryHigh-priority parser-inserted stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical bundles, remove redirects, and audit preload/script priorities around the LCP.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 432 KiB unused JavaScript and 241 KiB unused CSS; one store-assistant bundle wasted about 327 KiB and a UHF stylesheet was 98% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split the store assistant, conditionally load it after intent, and produce template-specific CSS bundles.

findings.summary: Some rendered images lack text alternatives.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 7 of 26 images without alt text, including a visible Azure AI content-card image; Lighthouse’s sampled load still scored automated accessibility at 1.0.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful linked/content images concise alt text and explicit empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: The homepage emits runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a ReimagineTelemetry ReferenceError, a querySelectorAllDeep TypeError, and two missing font resources (404).
findings.suggestedFix: Fix initialization ordering, remove the undefined deep-query dependency, and correct or remove the missing font URLs.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all 26 img elements lacked width and height attributes, with 3 oversized images and 16 lacking srcset; observed CLS happened to remain low in this run.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and responsive srcset/sizes for raster content.

findings.summary: An unload handler blocks the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s BFCache audit reports UnloadHandlerExistsInMainFrame.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload work with pagehide/visibilitychange where needed and verify BFCache restoration.

findings.summary: The organisation homepage lacks structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found zero JSON-LD blocks. Open Graph title, description, URL and type are present, and raw-HTML discoverability is strong.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD matching the visible brand and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers and cookie protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no CSP or X-Content-Type-Options; cookie inspection found ak_bmsc and bStore without Secure and all three sampled cookies using SameSite=None. HSTS is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP, nosniff, and Secure cookies with the narrowest viable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Clickjacking, referrer, and permissions defenses are absent on the main response.
findings.evidence: The main response had neither frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options nor Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, a strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for the script-heavy surface.

findings.summary: The default load has a broad analytics and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 11 third-party origins and active Microsoft Clarity endpoints; HAR attributes 49 requests and 1.18 MB to third-party origins before consent interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional analytics until consent, reduce third-party origins, and batch/minimise telemetry.

findings.summary: The app-like commerce experience has no install/offline declaration.
findings.evidence: Recon found no web app manifest, while the surface includes account, cart, assistant and shopping flows; no offline fallback was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a manifest and a lightweight service-worker fallback for navigation and saved shopping context.

findings.summary: Network/upstream failure handling degrades to a generic dead end.
findings.evidence: The product archetype was replaced by a generic high-demand page with no retry, stale product content, or alternate route.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve cached product details and explicit retry/category recovery when origin capacity fails.

findings.summary: The localized homepage does not use logical CSS properties in inspected styles.
findings.evidence: The document correctly declares lang=en-GB, but the rendered stylesheet probe found zero margin-inline, padding-inline, inset-inline, or inline-size matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate layout-critical physical left/right properties to logical inline/block properties and test RTL locales.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently resource-efficient.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 3 oversized images, 16 images without responsive sources, no detected modern-format images, and one legacy PNG; all 26 omitted intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where appropriate with srcset/sizes and right-size decorative images.

findings.summary: The default page load performs disproportionate work.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 197 requests, 140 scripts and 3.01 MB, while Lighthouse estimated 432 KiB unused JS and 241 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load commerce assistant and telemetry code after user intent; remove unused template CSS and duplicate runtime work.

findings.summary: Third-party resources consume a large share of the initial budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins accounted for 49 requests and 1.18 MB, including consent, UHF and analytics resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer optional vendors until consent or intent, and self-host stable critical assets where appropriate.
